title: 1951 AHSME Problem 43
statement: Of the following statements, the only one that is incorrect is:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
An inequality will remain true after each side is increased,
decreased, multiplied, or divided (zero excluded) by the same
positive quantity.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
The arithmetic mean of two unequal positive quantities is
greater than their geometric mean.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
If the sum of two positive quantities is given, their product
is largest when they are equal.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
If \(a\) and \(b\) are positive and unequal,
\(\dfrac12(a^2+b^2)\) is greater than
\(\left[\dfrac12(a+b)\right]^2.\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
If the product of two positive quantities is
given, their sum is greatest when they are equal.

solutions.text:
If \(uv=P\gt0,\) then \(u+v\ge2\sqrt P,\) with equality at \(u=v.\) Thus equality gives the least possible sum. The sum can grow without bound by taking \(u\) large and \(v=\frac{P}{u}\) small, so it is not greatest at equality.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: For a fixed positive product, compare the sum at equality with sums from increasingly unequal factors
AM-GM gives a minimum, not a maximum, for the sum when the product is fixed
